'''''Following''''' is a 1998 British [[Independent film|independent]] [[neo-noir]] film written, directed, photographed and edited by [[Christopher Nolan]] in his [[feature film]] [[directorial debut]]. He co-produced the film with his wife, [[Emma Thomas]], and actor [[Jeremy Theobald]]. Using a non-linear narrative, it tells the story of an aspiring writer (Theobald) who follows strangers around the streets of [[London]] and is drawn into a criminal underworld when he fails to keep his distance. 

Inspired by a burglary at his London flat, Nolan conceived ''Following'' as an "ultra-low budget" [[film noir]] and wrote the screenplay around resources at hand. As the crew consisted largely of Nolan's friends, all of whom held full-time jobs, principal photography took place exclusively on weekends across the course of a year. Much of the film was shot in the homes of Nolan's family and friends. Extensive rehearsals enabled scenes to be completed in a minimal amount of takes, which allowed the production to conserve expensive [[16 mm film]] stock. Nolan financed the production himself from his own salary working on corporate videos.

''Following'' screened at the 41st [[San Francisco International Film Festival]] on 24 April 1998. It was released on [[DVD]] and [[Blu-ray]] by [[The Criterion Collection]] in 2012.

==Plot==
<!--Plot summaries should should be between 400 and 700 words per MOS:FILM-->
A struggling, unemployed young writer (credited as "The Young Man") takes to following strangers around the streets of London, ostensibly to find inspiration for his first novel. Initially, he sets strict rules for himself regarding whom he should follow and for how long, but he soon discards them as he focuses on a well-groomed, handsome man in a dark suit. The man in the suit, having noticed he is being followed, quickly confronts the Young Man and introduces himself as "Cobb". Cobb reveals he is a serial burglar and invites the Young Man (who tells Cobb his name is "Bill") to accompany him on burglaries. The material gains from these crimes seem to be of secondary importance to Cobb. He takes pleasure in rifling through the personal items in his targets' flats and drinking their wine. He explains his true passion is using the shock of robbery, and violation of property, to make his victims re-examine their lives. He sums up his attitude thus: "You take it away, and show them what they had."

The Young Man is thrilled by Cobb's lifestyle. He attempts break-ins of his own, as Cobb encourages and guides him. At Cobb's suggestion, he alters his appearance, cutting his hair short and wearing a dark suit. He assumes the identity of "Daniel Lloyd", the name on the stolen credit card Cobb gives to him, and begins to pursue a relationship with a blonde woman whose flat he and Cobb burgled. The Blonde tells him she is the girlfriend of a small-time gangster, known only as the "Bald Guy", with whom she broke up after he and his gang murdered a man in her flat. Soon, the Blonde confides that the Bald Guy is blackmailing her with incriminating photographs. The Young Man breaks into the Bald Guy's safe but is caught in the act by a guard. He bludgeons the man with a hammer and flees with money and photos from the safe. Upon returning to his flat, he finds the photos are innocuous modelling shots.

Confronting the Blonde, the Young Man learns that she and Cobb have been working together to manipulate him into mimicking Cobb's burglary methods. She tells him that Cobb had recently discovered a murdered woman's body during one of his burglaries and that Cobb is attempting to deflect suspicion from himself by making it appear as though multiple burglars share his [[Modus operandi|MO]].

The Young Man leaves to turn himself in to the police. The Blonde reports her success to Cobb, who then reveals he actually works for the Bald Guy. The story about the murdered woman was part of a plot to deceive both the Blonde and the Young Man. The Blonde has been blackmailing the Bald Guy with evidence from the murder he committed in her flat, and he wants her killed in a way that cannot be connected to him. Cobb bludgeons the Blonde to death with the same hammer the Young Man used during the burglary of the Bald Guy's safe and leaves it at the scene. The police, checking out the Young Man's story, find the Blonde dead, the hammer with his fingerprints on it, and several other pieces of incriminating evidence. The Young Man is thus implicated in the murder of the Blonde. Meanwhile, Cobb vanishes.

Nolan's screenplay follows a non-linear plot structure, a device he has regularly used in his subsequent films. He initially scripted the story in chronological order with the intention of restructuring it during script editing. However, he found that he "had to do so much rewriting to make it coherent [and] make it flow for an audience", leading him to abandon that process for later projects.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Calhoun |first=Raquel |date=2024-02-23 |title=Christopher Nolan Explains Why He Doesn't Write His Nonlinear Scripts in Chronological Order |url=https://www.thewrap.com/christopher-nolan-writing-nonlinear-chronological-order-scripts/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723215736/https://www.thewrap.com/christopher-nolan-writing-nonlinear-chronological-order-scripts/ |archive-date=23 July 2025 |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[TheWrap]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The non-linear structure was partially motivated by the need to accommodate for a sporadic shooting schedule, which would make keeping continuity difficult.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":6" /> In 2002, Nolan stated: "In a compelling story of [<nowiki/>[[film noir]]] we are continually being asked to rethink our assessment of the relationship between the various characters, and I decided to structure my story in such a way as to emphasize the audience's incomplete understanding of each new scene as it is first presented."<ref name="nolandotnet">{{cite web|last=Duncker|first=Johannes|url=http://www.christophernolan.net/following_making.php|title=The Making of Following|date=6 June 2002|work=christophernolan.net|access-date=19 May 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513200348/http://www.christophernolan.net/following_making.php|archive-date=13 May 2008|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Alex Haw and [[Lucy Russell (actress)|Lucy Russell]], colleagues of Theobald from his university drama society, were cast in the two other major roles.<ref name="nolandotnet" /><ref name=":8" /> All three actors agreed not to cut their hair or leave the United Kingdom unexpectedly for the remainder of production, which was estimated at taking three months.<ref name="nolandotnet" /> The actors wore their own clothes in the film.<ref name="Ressner" /><ref name=":8" /> Nolan and the cast rehearsed two evenings a week for six months prior to filming.<ref name=":3" /><ref name="nolandotnet" /> These extensive rehearsals ensured the production could efficiently shoot scenes in the short amount of time that they had access to locations. It also meant that expensive film stock could be conserved by only using the first or second take in the final [[Film editing|edit]].<ref name="nolandotnet" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ncCEGQ82RKc |title=Christopher Nolan - Interview about 'Following' |date=2018-01-08 |last= |access-date=2026-07-21 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Nolan shot about fifteen minutes of raw footage each day.<ref name="Ressner" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tobias |first=Scott |date=5 June 2002 |title=Christopher Nolan |url=https://www.avclub.com/christopher-nolan-1798208223 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022133056/https://www.avclub.com/christopher-nolan-1798208223 |archive-date=22 October 2019 |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He estimated the [[shooting ratio]] as 3:1.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pulver |first=Andrew |date=1999-11-05 |title=A cult Following |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/1999/nov/05/2 |access-date=2026-07-21 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721035336/https://www.theguardian.com/film/1999/nov/05/2|archive-date=2026-07-21|url-status=live}}</ref> Thomas described the core crew as "about six to ten people... whoever was around".<ref name=":6" /> The cast and crew were sufficiently small that they could travel together in a single taxi when moving between filming locations.<ref name="nolandotnet" /><ref name=":8" /> Production was halted after Haw shaved his head, resuming once his hair had grown back.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":8" /> In the intervening time, Nolan directed a short film titled ''[[Doodlebug (film)|Doodlebug]]'' (1997),<ref name=":8" /> starring Theobald and co-produced by Thomas.<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Nordine |first=Michael |date=2016-07-17 |title=Christopher Nolan’s First Released Short Film ‘Doodlebug’: Watch His Twisted 1997 Debut |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/christopher-nolan-doodlebug-first-film-jeremy-theobald-1201706870/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[IndieWire]] |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721090225/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/christopher-nolan-doodlebug-first-film-jeremy-theobald-1201706870/|archive-date=2026-07-21|url-status=live}}</ref>

Filming mainly took place in the London flats of Nolan's friends.<ref name="nolandotnet" /> The Young Man's flat was Theobald's real-life flat,<ref name=":10" /> and the main house seen in the film was Nolan's parents' house.<ref name="nolandotnet" /> His mother provided sandwiches to the production team as [[catering]].<ref name="nolandotnet" /><ref name="Ressner" /> According to Nolan: "The only hitch came when the house was burgled and ironically enough, some of the items which are stolen in one of our fictional burglaries, were stolen in real life", which made certain [[Insert (filmmaking)|insert shots]] impossible to shoot.<ref name="nolandotnet" /> Additionally, the Bald Guy uses a hammer because a sufficiently realistic gun prop could not be sourced with the budget.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":8" /> 

Nolan shot ''Following'' with [[Arri]] BL and [[Bolex]] cameras<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":0" /> on [[16 mm film|16mm]] [[film stock]]. He chose to shoot in black-and-white to tap into the film noir genre as well as to hide budgetary constraints, reasoning that colour cinematography was harder to achieve on a low budget.<ref name=":3" /><ref name="nolandotnet" /> He stated that black-and-white cinematography made it quicker and easier to create a stylised look using light and shadow and eliminated the need to match light colour.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /> The handheld "documentary" style camerawork allowed Nolan to be spontaneous in blocking scenes.<ref name="nolandotnet" /><ref name=":0" /> He employed [[available light]] by staging many scenes next to windows.<ref name=":0" /> Additionally, Nolan identified the production's limitations in advance and incorporated them into the screenplay. He deliberately staged the opening police station scene in his college's film society using a [[Camera dolly|dolly]] shot and controlled lighting, which established early on that the film's later use of handheld camerawork was a deliberate stylistic choice rather than the result of inexperience or budgetary constraints.<ref name=":0" />

''Following'' ultimately took fourteen weekends<ref name=":6" /> over the course of a year to complete.<ref name="nolandotnet" /><ref name="Ressner" /> Nolan called the long production period "a blessing in disguise" as he was able to pay for film stock and processing without getting into debt.<ref name="nolandotnet" />

=== Editing ===
Nolan began syncing the film's rushes about six months into filming: "I found a place that was prepared to give me a little time to learn the machines for free, and beyond that I had to start paying for it." Nolan rented a machine for £100 over a weekend, and completed the rough cut over the course of three weekends.<ref name=":6" /> He enlisted the help of his university friend Gareth Heal; Nolan and Heal ultimately co-edited the film.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":5" /> ''Following'' was originally edited on [[U-matic|U-matic tape]], and then digitally edited on [[Media Composer|Avid Media Composer]] by Heal.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":0" />

After a screening for cast and crew, the first act of the film was re-edited to play more chronologically.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":6" /> Once ''Following'' was accepted to film festivals, Heal and Nolan sought finances to reassemble the edit on a [[Negative (photography)|film negative]] struck from the 16mm film stock.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> The production team received finishing funds from the [[Independent Film Channel]]'s [[Next Wave Films]] to print the feature on [[35 mm movie film|35 mm film]].<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |last= |date=1998-09-17 |title=October and Rohmer; Next Wave’s “Following”; The 24 Hour Festival; and Air Canada is Back |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/october-and-rohmer-next-waves-following-the-24-hour-festival-and-air-canada-is-back-82595/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[IndieWire]] |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721041835/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/october-and-rohmer-next-waves-following-the-24-hour-festival-and-air-canada-is-back-82595/|archive-date=2026-07-21|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release==
''Following'' screened at the 41st [[San Francisco International Film Festival]] on 24 April 1998.<ref>{{cite web |date=21 December 2014 |title=41st San Francisco International Film Festival at PFA |url=https://bampfa.org/program/41st-san-francisco-international-film-festival-pfa |access-date=24 January 2022 |publisher=[[The Regents of the University of California]]}}</ref><ref name="Ressner" /> It was later distributed by [[Zeitgeist Films]].<ref name="Ressner" />

A [[Blu-ray]] and [[DVD]] restoration of the film with a new 5.1 sound mix was released by [[The Criterion Collection]] for [[Blu-ray#Region codes|Region A]] on 11 December 2012. Both the Blu-ray and DVD include a commentary by and an interview with Nolan, a chronological edit of the film, a side-by-side comparison between three scenes of the film and the shooting script, Nolan's 1997 short film ''[[Doodlebug (film)|Doodlebug]]'', and both the theatrical and re-release trailers. Each edition contains an essay by film critic [[Scott Foundas]], titled "Nolan Begins". Exclusive to the Blu-ray is an [[Audio file format#Uncompressed audio format|uncompressed]] [[monaural]] soundtrack to the film.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.criterion.com/films/28030-following|title=Criterion – Following|publisher=[[The Criterion Collection]]|access-date=15 July 2017|archive-date=7 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107060854/https://www.criterion.com/films/28030-following|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Atanasov|first1=Svet|title=Following Blu-ray Review|url=http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Following-Blu-ray/55340/#Review|website=Blu-ray.com|access-date=15 July 2017|date=2 December 2012|archive-date=11 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170711143008/http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Following-Blu-ray/55340/#Review|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Foundas |first=Scott |date=12 December 2012 |title=Following: Nolan Begins |url=https://www.criterion.com/current/posts/2596-following-nolan-begins |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[The Criterion Collection]] |language=en|author-link=Scott Foundas|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260305000934/https://www.criterion.com/current/posts/2596-following-nolan-begins|archive-date=5 March 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Reception==

=== Critical response ===

==== Contemporary ====
''Following'' garnered positive critical reception.<ref name=":14" /> ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' reviewer Kevin Thomas was particularly impressed by the "taut and ingenious neo-noir", stating that "as a psychological mystery it plays persuasively if not profoundly. Nolan relishes the sheer nastiness he keeps stirred up, unabated for 70 minutes."<ref name="latimesreview">{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-jun-04-ca-43950-story.html |title=Following: 'Following' the Twisting Path of Sinister, Neo Noir Intrigue |last=Thomas |first=Kevin |date=4 June 1999 |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=19 July 2009 |archive-date=5 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105175021/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/jun/04/entertainment/ca-43950 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The New Yorker]]'' wrote that ''Following'' echoed [[Alfred Hitchcock|Hitchcock]] classics but was "leaner and meaner".<ref name="NewYorker">{{cite magazine |last1=Diones |first1=Bruce |title=Following |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=19 April 1999 |url=http://archives.newyorker.com/default.aspx?iid=15470&startpage=page0000021#folio=018 |page=19 |access-date=20 February 2019 |archive-date=20 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220181421/http://archives.newyorker.com/default.aspx?iid=15470&startpage=page0000021#folio=018 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[TV Guide]]'' called it "short, sharp and tough as nails", praising its fast-paced storytelling and "tricky, triple-tiered flashback structure."<ref name="tvguidereview">{{cite news|last=Fox|first=Ken|url=http://www.tvguide.com/movies/following/review/134067|title=Following: Review|work=[[TV Guide]]|access-date=19 May 2008|archive-date=14 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414072054/http://www.tvguide.com/movies/following/review/134067/|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Janet Maslin]], in a review for ''[[The New York Times]]'', highlighted the film's non-linear structure.<ref name=":12" /> David Thompson of ''[[Sight and Sound]]'' commented that "Nolan shows a natural talent for a fluent handheld aesthetic."<ref name="Sight_and_Sound_review">{{cite web|url=http://www.bfi.org.uk/sightandsound/review/266|title=Following (1998)|date=December 1999|first=David|last=Thompson|work=Sight and Sound|access-date=19 July 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205114801/http://www.bfi.org.uk/sightandsound/review/266|archive-date=5 December 2008|df=dmy-all|publisher=[[British Film Institute]]}}</ref> Jonathan Romney of [[New Statesmen]] praised Nolan's "disorienting" urban depiction of London, and compared his filmmaking to [[Nicolas Roeg]] and [[Chris Petit]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Romney |first=Jonathan |date=1 January 1999 |title=Cheap thrills |url=http://www.newstatesman.com/199911080043 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111053121/http://www.newstatesman.com/199911080043 |archive-date=11 January 2011 |access-date=17 December 2011 |work=[[New Statesman]] |location=}}</ref> Stephen Garrett, writing for [[IndieWire]], called the film a "major highlight" of "inspired drama".<ref name=":14" />

However, [[Tony Rayns]] felt that the film's climax was uninspired, saying that "the generic pay off is a little disappointing after the edgy, character based scenes of exposition".<ref name="timeoutreview">{{cite web|last=Rayns|first=Tony|author-link=Tony Rayns|url=http://www.timeout.com/film/reviews/66855/following.html|title=Following|publisher=[[Time Out (company)|Time Out]]|access-date=19 July 2009|archive-date=29 June 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629074901/http://www.timeout.com/film/reviews/66855/following.html|url-status=live|date=3 May 2011}}</ref> ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s Trevor Lewis questioned the skill of the film's inexperienced cast, saying that they "lack the dramatic ballast to compensate for [Nolan's] erratic plot elisions."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Trevor |date=2000 |title=Following |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/following-review/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201182721/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/following-review/ |archive-date=1 February 2026 |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |language=en}}</ref> Dennis Harvey of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' felt the British film was compromised by its "Amerindie feel", stating the limited depths of the characters didn't justify its grittiness. He believed its narrative "might work better in a more commercial framework".<ref name=":11" /> In contrast, David Thompson was of the opinion that the "unfamiliar cast acquit themselves well in a simple naturalistic style."<ref name="Sight_and_Sound_review" />

==== Retrospective ====
''Following'' received generally positive reviews. The film has an [[approval rating]] of 87% on [[Rotten Tomatoes]] based on 89 reviews, with an average rating of 7.30/10. The site's critical consensus reads, "Super brief but efficient, ''Following'' represents director Christopher Nolan's burgeoning talent in tight filmmaking and hard-edge noir."<ref name="rottentomatoes">{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/following/ |title=Following (1999) |website=Rotten Tomatoes |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=7 July 2026 |archive-date=29 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171129072559/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/following/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a weighted average score of 60 out of 100 based on 11 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metacritic.com/movie/following |title=Following Reviews |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=31 July 2018 |archive-date=22 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722053237/http://www.metacritic.com/movie/following |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2007, filmmaker [[Joel Schumacher]] praised ''Following'' as the work of a "brilliant" young director. "I always had him in the back of my mind, thinking, 'We're going to hear from this guy, big time.' Then I saw ''Memento'' and the promise was fulfilled very fast."<ref name="Schumacher11">{{cite web|url=https://www.ifc.com/2011/10/joel-schumacher-christopher-nolan-the-dark-knight-rises-batman|title=Joel Schumacher explains why he isn't surprised by Christopher Nolan's "The Dark Knight" success|first=Rick|last=Marshall|work=Ifc.com|access-date=22 June 2020|archive-date=8 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908202254/http://www.ifc.com/2011/10/joel-schumacher-christopher-nolan-the-dark-knight-rises-batman|url-status=dead|date=10 October 2007}}</ref>

Critics have noted that ''Following'' is an early example of Nolan's trademark use of a non-linear plot structure.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=2012-12-14 |title=Following: Nolan in a nutshell |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/following-nolan-in-a-nutshell |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |language=en-US|last=Emerson|first=Jim}}</ref> In 2012, Jim Emerson of [[RogerEbert.com]] stated that the film "shows the Nolan we now know almost fully formed".<ref name=":7" /> The name Cobb was reused for a character in Nolan's 2010 film ''[[Inception]]''.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7" /> In 2020, Matt Goldberg of ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' noted that ''Following'' introduces themes that Nolan would continue to explore in his later films.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Matt |date=2020-08-17 |title=How ‘Following’ Laid the Foundation of Christopher Nolan’s Filmography |url=https://collider.com/christopher-nolan-following-movie-explained/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref> Siddhant Adlakha of ''[[IGN]]'' described the film as an early example of Nolan's thematic exploration of obsession and "logic vs impulse". Adlakha wrote that the film's characters evoke classic film noir archetypes, but that the "disorienting narrative" sets ''Following'' apart from a typical film noir. He also compared certain scenes to the 1945 film noir ''[[Detour (1945 film)|Detour]]'' and the 1964 [[List of James Bond films|James Bond film]] ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]''.<ref name=":5" />

''Following'' has since been recognized as one of the most notable [[no budget film|no-budget films]] of its time.<ref name="TheVine">{{cite web|url=http://www.thevine.com.au/entertainment/top10/top-ten-films-made-on-a-shoestring-budget/|title=Top ten films made on a shoestring budget|first=Scott|last=Henderson|work=TheVine|access-date=24 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120824232338/http://www.thevine.com.au/entertainment/top10/top-ten-films-made-on-a-shoestring-budget|archive-date=24 August 2012|url-status=dead|date=26 November 2010}}</ref> Several members of ''Following''<nowiki/>'s cast and crew went on to collaborate with Nolan on his later films, such as composer [[David Julyan]],<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":15" /> producer Emma Thomas,<ref name=":4" /> and actors Jeremy Theobald,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ftvdb.bfi.org.uk/sift/individual/776218?view=credit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071112043209/http://ftvdb.bfi.org.uk/sift/individual/776218?view=credit|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 November 2007|title=Filmography: THEOBALD, Jeremy|publisher=[[British Film Institute]]|date=16 April 2009|access-date=17 December 2011}}</ref> John Nolan,<ref name=":13">{{Cite news |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/john-nolan-dies-87-1236858232/|title=John Nolan Dies: 'Dark Knight Rises' & 'Person of Interest' Actor Was 87|last=Garner|first=Glenn|date=11 April 2026|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=11 April 2026|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260412000004/https://deadline.com/2026/04/john-nolan-dies-87-1236858232/|archive-date=12 April 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> and Lucy Russell.<ref name=":8" />

===Accolades===
''Following'' won several awards during its festival run, including the Tiger Award at the [[International Film Festival Rotterdam]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.filmfestivalrotterdam.com/en/about/awards-and-jury/tiger-awards/previous-winners/ |title=Tiger Awards Competition: previous winners |publisher=International Film Festival Rotterdam |access-date=2013-02-12 |archive-date=21 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130121013119/http://www.filmfestivalrotterdam.com/en/about/awards-and-jury/tiger-awards/previous-winners/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the "Best First Feature" prize at the [[San Francisco International Film Festival]], among others. ''Following'' also won the Black and White award as well as a Grand Jury Prize nomination at [[Slamdance Film Festival]].<ref>[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0154506/awards?ref_=tt_awd "Awards for Following"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305114054/https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0154506/awards?ref_=tt_awd |date=5 March 2016 }}. ''[[IMDb]]''. Retrieved 25 June 2013.</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=August 2026}}
